public_rationale: The human model-building component is supported within a controlled task: research published September 22, 2020 reported that participants used learned graph structure to infer unobserved paths [e3]. Some LLM memorization is also supported: a preprint posted December 14, 2020 reported extracting hundreds of verbatim training sequences from GPT-2 [e1]. The implied exclusion of relational representations from LLM behavior is challenged by Anthropic's March 27, 2025 report: intervening on Claude's intermediate representation changed its answer from Austin to Sacramento, indicating that the intermediate step affected the answer [e2]. These findings support human structural learning and some LLM memorization, but do not establish memorization as a sufficient explanation of the tested Claude behavior [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The assessment interprets the contrast as excluding relational model building in LLMs; the statement does not explicitly say 'only'.
The GPT-2 results do not establish memorization of the entire internet or explain all LLM behavior [e1].
The Claude intervention is reported by its developer. The packet provides no independent replication, and the example does not establish equivalence to human cognition [e2].
The human evidence supplied is an abstract covering graph-learning experiments. It does not give experimental session dates or establish a comprehensive account of human learning [e3].
The evidence does not quantify an 'immense' overall difference between human and LLM mechanisms [e1, e2, e3].

I treat 'the entire internet' as rhetorical breadth, rather than requiring literal storage of every internet page.
